title: Requirements register
note: Every requirement from the project brief, mapped to where it is met in this repository and to the official Kalshi source that supports the claim. Status values: implemented, partial, blocked, open, not verified. A row is only 'implemented' when the code and the official evidence both exist.

requirements.requirement: Collect, organize and analyse the project against a full list of requirements.
requirements.evidence_label: demo environment (API surface the register describes)
requirements.note: The register is the artefact; each row links the official endpoint or documentation page the claim rests on.

requirements.requirement: Produce an executive summary of the important details.
requirements.note: A second executive summary also exists in the intelligence subsite; both are kept.

requirements.requirement: A dashboard that tracks the highest dollar amount of live events, limited to gas prices, elections, culture, crypto and golf.
requirements.note: The API publishes no dollar-volume field, so each row shows the official contract volume plus a clearly labelled estimate computed as volume_24h_fp x last_price_dollars.

requirements.requirement: Keep tracking live events until they resolve, and record how each resolved, yes or no.
requirements.where_label: Gas page (same layout on every topic page)
requirements.note: The official result field carries yes or no; 1,601 settled in-scope markets are shown with their result.

requirements.requirement: Automate simulated trades to test different strategies.
requirements.note: Simulated trades need no credential and are scored against the official settlement result.

requirements.requirement: Track portfolio performance on the Kalshi demo account.
requirements.note: Balance, positions and fills need a signed request with an API key. No key exists in this repository, so the values stay blank and flagged rather than being filled in.

requirements.requirement: Analyse trade results, categorise the trades and create strategies per trade type.
requirements.note: Categorisation axes are topic, side, price band and topic x side. A bucket needs 10 trades before a pattern is described.

requirements.requirement: Execute trades on events and track the performance.
requirements.note: The V2 endpoint POST /portfolio/events/orders is implemented behind three gates. The legacy endpoint returns 410 Gone and is not used. Execution cannot run until a demo key pair exists.

requirements.requirement: A live interactive graph of contract price movement: X axis time with a selectable length in seconds, minutes or hours, Y axis the current contract price.
requirements.note: Windows of 60 s, 5 min, 15 min, 1 h, 6 h, 24 h, 7 d and 30 d. Short windows use the trade prints, longer windows use the documented 1, 60 and 1440 minute candlesticks.

requirements.requirement: Show current liquidity: how many contracts are available at a given price.
requirements.note: Kalshi publishes yes bids and no bids only, so the ask ladder is derived from the no bids as 1 - p and is labelled as derived.

requirements.requirement: Suggestions on how to make the site more live and interactive, with simplified graphs and charts.
requirements.note: The websocket handshake needs signed headers, so a static page cannot subscribe to it; that constraint is what the suggestions are measured against.

requirements.requirement: Live charts should show the events and website links that may have caused a sharp jump in contract price of $0.10 or more in either direction.
requirements.where_label: Sharp move monitor (also on the repository dashboard)
requirements.note: The moves and their official source are detected and shown, both in the consolidated desk and on the repository dashboard, where a red marker is drawn on the live chart. The cause cannot be verified because the Kalshi Trade API publishes no news feed, so that column is left empty and flagged. The links shown are the settlement references Kalshi itself names for the series.

requirements.requirement: Keep the topics separate while keeping the events inside one topic together, and simplify the site so a trader can decide from it.
requirements.note: Topics are separated using the official category and tags filters, with one page per topic and the events inside a topic kept together. The seven dashboards built by parallel sessions are now grouped on a second navigation row so the primary bar stays short.

requirements.requirement: No manual input from the operator: the collection, verification and publication run on their own.
requirements.note: Collection runs on a schedule from a runner with outbound access; the rate-limit document explains the backoff the collector uses.

requirements.requirement: Review the repository line by line, verify from official trusted sources, provide links for manual review and flag irregularities.
requirements.note: The verification page adds a machine-checked audit: every data row must carry an official Kalshi URL, and a sample is re-fetched from the live API and compared with the committed snapshot.

requirements.requirement: A GitHub Pages site with a clean landing page and subpages organised by category, holding every entry and finding in simple readable tables.
requirements.note: One landing page, one page per topic, and pages for sharp moves, trading, requirements, verification and flagged items. Every table row carries its official source.

requirements.requirement: Every table row must have a source link to an official site; a value that cannot be confirmed is left blank and flagged, never inferred.
requirements.note: Blank portfolio values, unverified cause columns and the absent culture rows are all stated as such on the pages themselves.

requirements.requirement: Coordinate parallel sessions through a shared task board with claims, sources and recorded irregularities.
requirements.note: This row describes repository process rather than a Kalshi fact, so it links the repository itself.
